name: Yaman
aarohana: N. R G M+ D N S'
avarohana: S' N D P M+ G R S
pakad: N. R G R S, P M+ G R S
characteristicMovements: Frequently begins from Mandra Ni (N.) bypassing Sa in ascent (N. R G M+ D N S'), features gentle glides onto Tivra Ma (M+), and resolves through G R S.
musicalCharacteristics: All seven notes are Shuddha except Tivra Madhyama (M+). Considered a foundational evening raga of Kalyan Thaat with expansive serenity.
performanceTime: First quarter of the night (approx. 6 PM – 9 PM)
sourceNote: Standard Hindustani musicological canon (Bhatkhande Kalyan Thaat taxonomy).

name: Bhairav
aarohana: S r G M P d N S'
avarohana: S' N d P M G r S
pakad: G M d P, G M r S
characteristicMovements: Pronounced slow oscillation (Andolan) on Komal Re (r) and Komal Dha (d), with characteristic phrases moving from Ma to Komal Dha and resolving via G M r S.
musicalCharacteristics: Sampurna-Sampurna heptatonic raga employing Komal Re and Komal Dha alongside Shuddha Ga and Shuddha Ni, creating stark intervals around Sa and Pa.

name: Bhupali
aarohana: S R G P D S'
avarohana: S' D P G R S
pakad: G R S D. S R G, P G D P G R S
characteristicMovements: Audava-Audava pentatonic structure omitting Ma and Ni completely; uses graceful meend glides between Ga, Pa, and Dha.
musicalCharacteristics: All five notes are Shuddha. Shares identical scalar pitch-classes with Deshkar (which belongs to Bilawal Thaat and emphasizes Dha and upper tetrachord), making melodic phrase distinction essential.

name: Malkauns
aarohana: S g M d n S'
avarohana: S' n d M g S
pakad: M g M d n d M, g S
characteristicMovements: Omits Re and Pa entirely; anchors heavily on Shuddha Ma and Mandra Komal Ni (n.) with deep, deliberate glides across minor-third and fourth intervals.
musicalCharacteristics: Audava-Audava pentatonic raga using Komal Ga, Komal Dha, and Komal Ni, evoking meditative gravity.

name: Bhimpalasi
aarohana: n. S g M P n S'
avarohana: S' n D P M g R S
pakad: n. S M, M g P M, g M g R S
characteristicMovements: Audava in ascent (omits Re and Dha), Sampurna in descent; approaches Komal Ga from Ma via delicate Kan/Meend and rests strongly on Ma and Sa.
musicalCharacteristics: Audava-Sampurna raga of Kafi Thaat combining pentatonic ascent with full heptatonic descent.

name: Desh
aarohana: S R M P N S'
avarohana: S' n D P M G R G N. S
pakad: R M P N S' R' n D P, M G R
characteristicMovements: Uses Shuddha Ni in direct ascent to upper Sa (R M P N S') and Komal Ni in descent (S' n D P), with recurring emphasis on Re and Pa.
musicalCharacteristics: Audava-Sampurna raga of Khamaj Thaat featuring dual Ni usage (Ubhay Nishad).
performanceTime: Second quarter of the night (approx. 9 PM – 12 AM)

name: Kafi
aarohana: S R g M P D n S'
avarohana: S' n D P M g R S
pakad: S R g M P, M P D P g R S
characteristicMovements: Stepwise linear and vakra phrases centered on Re-Ga(k)-Ma-Pa, occasionally touching Shuddha Ga or Shuddha Ni in light-classical renditions.
musicalCharacteristics: Sampurna-Sampurna foundational raga of Kafi Thaat; widely used in both Khayal and Thumri/Dadra forms.
performanceTime: Late night / Evening (Gharana traditions vary; seasonal association with Holi)

name: Darbari Kanada
aarohana: S R g M P d n S'
avarohana: S' d n P, M P g M R S
pakad: g~ R S, d. n. S R, M P d n P
characteristicMovements: Slow, weighty Andolan (wide oscillation) on Komal Ga and Komal Dha, plus signature Kanada descending turn (g M R S) and oblique phrases in lower-middle octave.
musicalCharacteristics: Deeply ornamented raga of Asavari Thaat where Gamaka and slow tempo (Vilambit) are essential structural identifiers.

name: Kalyani (Mechakalayani)
aarohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S'
avarohana: S' N3 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
vadi: Pending verification (Carnatic Graha/Jeeva Svara conventions differ from Hindustani Vadi)
pakad: N3 R2 G3 M2 D2 N3 S' (Characteristic Carnatic Sanchara)
characteristicMovements: Rich kampita gamakas on G3, D2, and N3; luminous upper-tetrachord sancharas starting from M2 or P.
musicalCharacteristics: 65th Melakarta raga in the 72-Melakarta Carnatic scheme; major auspicious raga with Prati Madhyama.
performanceTime: Evening / Concert repertoire (time-theory constraints are less rigid in Carnatic practice)
sourceNote: Carnatic Melakarta taxonomy; kept separate from Hindustani classifier scope.

name: Mayamalavagowla
aarohana: S r1 G3 M1 P d1 N3 S'
avarohana: S' N3 d1 P M1 G3 r1 S
pakad: S r1 G3 M1 P, d1 N3 S'
characteristicMovements: Foundational beginner pedagogical scale in Carnatic music with symmetrical r1-G3 and d1-N3 intervals.
musicalCharacteristics: 15th Melakarta raga; structural counterpart to Hindustani Bhairav in scale degrees, though differentiated by Carnatic gamaka grammar.
sourceNote: 72-Melakarta Carnatic pedagogical canon; excluded from Hindustani classifier.

name: Mohanam
aarohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S'
avarohana: S' D2 P G3 R2 S
vadi: Pending verification (Carnatic Jeeva Svara: G3, P, D2)
pakad: G3 P D2 P G3 R2 S
characteristicMovements: Pentatonic Audava raga featuring expressive jaru glides and subtle kampita on Gandhara and Dhaivata.
musicalCharacteristics: Symmetric pentatonic Carnatic raga; shares pitch set with Hindustani Bhupali but differs in phrasing and gamaka articulation.
sourceNote: Carnatic Janya Raga taxonomy; kept separate from Hindustani classifier.

name: Hamsadhwani
aarohana: S R2 G3 P N3 S'
avarohana: S' N3 P G3 R2 S
vadi: Pending verification (Carnatic Jeeva Svara: R2, G3, N3)
pakad: S R2 G3 P N3 P G3 R2 S
characteristicMovements: Energetic pentatonic phrases omitting Ma and Dha, often opened with bright N3-S'-R2 leaps.
musicalCharacteristics: Auspicious Carnatic raga frequently performed as an opening concert piece; also adopted in Hindustani concerts.
sourceNote: Carnatic Janya Raga canon (attributed to Ramaswami Dikshitar); excluded from Hindustani classifier.
